clue.text: One of eight who survive if Stalin is transformed by mercy

parts.note: to give quarter is to show mercy to a defeated enemy

indicators.note: the letters of 'if Stalin' are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dictator is changed by a show of mercy and lives on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalin' sets up a political surface, but with 'if' it is anagram fodder; 'by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The last eight in a knockout tournament each play in the round before the semis, having survived earlier rounds.

clue.text: Game to make one flinch

definitions.meaning: a small game bird shot for sport and food
in older English the verb could be used transitively, meaning to daunt or cow someone

explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a classic game species, and the verb means to cower or lose heart.

clue.text: Star a man is about to exclude

indicators.note: the man's name is placed around the other piece, as if surrounding it

parts.note: Alan is a man's name
to debar is to exclude or shut out

explanation.surface: A celebrity is a man on the point of being kept out.
explanation.definitionFit: The brightest star in the constellation Taurus bears this Arabic name.

clue.text: Food which is beginning without a beginning

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped from the synonym of the earlier word

parts.note: a beginning is a start

explanation.surface: A dish that has no starting point, though it is itself a start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a beginning' drops the S from START.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry case with a sweet filling is a dish to eat.

clue.text: Town which has a crop of good scores?

definitions.text: Town which has a crop of good scores?

parts.words: Town which has a crop of good scores?
parts.note: read as a crop, like wheat, whose harvest is cricket scores: a 'crop' of scores in the batting sense

explanation.surface: A place blessed with lots of high marks.
explanation.walkthrough: RUNCORN is a town in Cheshire, northwest England; the question mark warns the clue splits it into RUN (a cricket score) and CORN (a crop).
explanation.definitionFit: This is an industrial town on the River Mersey in Cheshire.

clue.text: A penny is nice when recast and engraved

indicators.note: metal that is recast is melted and shaped anew, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for an old British penny, from the Latin denarius

explanation.surface: A coin looks good once it has been reminted and stamped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when recast' rearranges ISNICE into INCISE, then D for penny follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cut into a surface with a sharp tool has been carved or engraved.

clue.text: Provide weapons before there is trouble about sick animal

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the rest in the answer

parts.note: to arm is to supply with weapons

indicators.note: the fuss word is wrapped around the word for unwell

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Arm yourself before trouble breaks out over an ailing beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing American mammal covered in bony armour plates.

clue.text: Juice which means one job is cut short

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the last letter is lopped off the word for a task

parts.note: a chore is a routine job

explanation.surface: A drink whose name suggests a single unfinished task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is cut short' trims CHORE to CHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was the fluid flowing in the gods' veins, hence also a watery discharge or juice.

clue.text: Fatigue gives one sore appearance after start of training

indicators.note: the pieces named before this word follow the first letter
only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a sore patch of skin looks inflamed, showing redness

explanation.surface: Exhaustion shows as aching red skin once a training regime begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Weariness and exhaustion are the state of being worn out.

clue.text: Dog in addition to club

parts.note: and means plus, in addition to
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A canine along with a golf club, ready for a round.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog is a metal support for logs in a hearth, also called a dog.

clue.text: Kind of oil which would give speed in a vehicle if nothing were missing

indicators.note: the speed and nought sit inside the word for a vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A motoring note about speed and an incomplete vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Speed in a vehicle alone falls one letter short; 'if nothing were missing' tells you the zero must be added alongside the speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A waxy aromatic substance obtained as an oil from the camphor laurel.

clue.text: Projection of the earth without gravity

indicators.note: the letter for gravity is removed from the planet word

parts.note: the globe is the earth
G is the symbol for gravity or its acceleration

explanation.surface: A protruding feature of a planet with no pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded projecting part, such as of the ear or a leaf.

clue.text: Thought the opposing team dangerous looking

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a side is a team
red is the colour of danger signals

explanation.surface: The opposition was judged to look threatening.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carefully weighed up or reflected upon has been pondered.

clue.text: Favourable transaction brings profit to the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
gain means profit

explanation.surface: A good deal earns money for the local.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal at a good price is a favourable purchase.

clue.text: In retreat the defender precedes those who need protection

indicators.note: the defender word comes first in the answer, ahead of the second piece

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or rugby
wards are people under the care of a guardian

explanation.surface: A defender stands in front of the vulnerable as the side falls back.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving in reverse, retreating, is going in the opposite direction.

clue.text: Current long-term prisoner without a single means of making his voice heard

definitions.text: means of making his voice heard

parts.note: amp, ampere, is the unit of electric current

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, the prisoner word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a lifer is serving a life sentence
I is one, a single

explanation.surface: An inmate serving life, alone, finds a way to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the prisoner surrounds the single letter rather than losing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that boosts sound so a speaker carries further.

clue.text: Conducted back to the river to get rid of vermin

indicators.note: the word for conducted is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: led means conducted or guided
the Ouse is a river in England (several rivers bear the name)

explanation.surface: Someone was escorted back to the riverside to deal with pests.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a person or animal of lice is to remove vermin.

clue.text: Revolutionary changes almost pull in universal friends

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing

indicators.note: the shortened pull goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: pals are friends

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped from the word for pull

parts.note: to heave is to pull hard

explanation.surface: Big upheavals nearly drag in friends from everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of the word for pull before it goes inside the universal and friends pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden violent disruptions overturn the existing order.

clue.text: Record a piece of music for a star

parts.note: to can is to record, as in a film being in the can
an opus is a musical work

explanation.surface: A musician lays down a track to become famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The second brightest star in the night sky, in the constellation Carina.

clue.text: Giant cactus or kind of palm seen around Arab countries

indicators.note: the palm word surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: the sago palm yields a starch
UAR is the United Arab Republic, the union of Egypt and Syria

explanation.surface: Desert plants found across the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge columnar cactus of the Sonoran Desert in the American Southwest.

clue.text: Surrounded by idiots a man makes garments

indicators.note: the man is enclosed within the word for fools

parts.note: clots are idiots, in British slang
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man in foolish company makes his own outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments are things worn to cover the body.

clue.text: Work with a hook when agitated after pot is unfinished

indicators.note: the agitated piece follows the shortened pot in the answer
the last letter of the pot word is dropped

parts.note: a crock is an earthenware pot
het, as in het up, means agitated

explanation.surface: Someone flustered after leaving a pot half-made takes up needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft of making fabric by looping yarn with a hooked needle.

clue.text: Saw nothing turned into capital

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are reshaped into something new

explanation.surface: Someone saw nothing that became a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat of the US federal government is the American capital city.

clue.text: Organisation which puts one in the lead at court?

definitions.meaning: an arrangement or structure, as in the way things are organised

definitions.text: puts one in the lead at court?
definitions.meaning: in tennis, being a set ahead of the opponent puts a player one set in front

explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement of parts is a structure, and in tennis one is a set ahead.

clue.text: Injury which is hard on a limb

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A damaged limb after a hard blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage or hurt done to someone.

clue.text: Fashions which are not quite decorous

indicators.note: the final letter is left off the word for decorous

parts.note: modest means decorous, seemly

explanation.surface: Styles that fall a little short of propriety.
explanation.definitionFit: Ways or styles of doing things, especially current trends.

clue.text: Illness which gives Andrew less cheek

indicators.note: the second word is subtracted from the surname

parts.note: Sir Andrew Aguecheek is the foolish knight in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night
taken as written

explanation.surface: A disease gives a man a less cheeky manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew stands for Sir Andrew Aguecheek of Twelfth Night; take CHEEK off his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A fever with shivering fits, often malarial.

clue.text: Retains mixed drink

indicators.note: the letters of the word are jumbled like a cocktail

explanation.surface: A mixed drink is kept back.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Rider looking gaunt

definitions.meaning: H. Rider ..., author of King Solomon's Mines

explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist shares the name, and the adjective means drawn and exhausted.

clue.text: Machines which are outstanding for locks

parts.note: super means excellent, outstanding
tresses are locks of hair

explanation.surface: Excellent devices made for hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boeing B-29 bombers of the Second World War were nicknamed by this name, warplanes being machines.
